criteria.text: With a committed changed test, a nonzero old-code exit containing the literal "defect-x" and a zero new-code exit produce a successful old-code proof and exit 0.
If the old code passes, or fails with "other-error" instead of "defect-x", the report distinguishes "old-passes" from "wrong-reason", includes the observed wrong-reason excerpt and exits 1.

If the new code fails, the report says "head-fails", includes the observed cause and short actual output tail before a trailing TAP summary when available and exits 1 even when the old code fails with "defect-x".

Each phase requests a 120-second limit, a 2-second process-group kill grace and a 1 MiB output cap; base timeout, head timeout, output overflow and child signals have distinct unsuccessful reports and exit 1.

No changed test gives "no-changed-tests"; missing commits, unsafe overlay setup, exit 126/127 and known missing-fixture/import failures give "setup-error" with a cause and short actual output tail when available even when output contains "defect-x"; setup-looking output from a passing phase does not disqualify proof.

The proof compares committed regular added, modified or renamed tests and supplemental files against the merge-base of HEAD with the fetched selected base branch, excluding base-branch changes already merged into HEAD, and ignores deleted files and implementation.

The v2 saved result keeps parent interruption separately from child signals, the computed old base and captured head, exact command and expectation, copied paths, phase exits, final output and observed excerpt; the immutable saved run base stays unchanged, cleanup always runs, and each report names the command and actual base/head exits with safe code spans preserving literal command quotes and backslashes with visible control escapes rather than claiming copied files were executed tests.
The quoted command "node --test test/new.test.mjs" and expectation "defect x" reach the proof unchanged; missing, duplicate or blank options and extra operands exit 2 before proof execution.
